decks.name: Neuropathology I: General, Development & Infection (Board Review)

zeilen: Extracellular, mainly **white matter**, enhances; **responds to steroids**
Intracellular, gray + white matter, **restricted diffusion**, no enhancement, no steroid response

cards.rueckseite:
**Red neuron:** irreversible ischemic injury: shrunken, hypereosinophilic cytoplasm, pyknotic nucleus; visible after **~6–12 h**. Ferrugination = old dead neurons encrusted with Ca/Fe.
**Central chromatolysis:** reaction to **axonal injury near the cell body**: swollen soma, loss of Nissl substance, **eccentric nucleus**; potentially reversible (e.g. anterior horn cells after root avulsion).

zeilen: Pilocytic astrocytoma, Alexander disease, chronic gliosis

cards.rueckseite:
**Hamartoma:** disorganized mature tissue native to that location (e.g. hypothalamic hamartoma, tuber).
**Choristoma:** normal tissue in an abnormal location (e.g. heterotopic glial tissue, granular cell tumor of the neurohypophysis historically).

- **Kernohan notch** (contralateral peduncle) → ipsilateral hemiparesis
- **PCA infarction** (occipital) from compression at the tentorial edge
- **Duret hemorrhages** in midbrain/pons (stretched perforators)
- **CN III palsy** (blown pupil)
- Aqueductal compression → hydrocephalus

**Astrocytes** (GFAP): reactive gliosis, gemistocytes; **Alzheimer type II astrocytes** in hepatic encephalopathy (hyperammonemia).
**Microglia:** resident macrophages (rod cells, microglial nodules in viral encephalitis).
**Oligodendrocytes:** enlarged bizarre nuclei with viral inclusions in **PML**.
**Ependyma:** does not regenerate (replaced by subependymal gliosis/granular ependymitis).

cards.vorderseite: Neural tube closure and neurulation timeline
cards.rueckseite:
Notochord day ~17 → neural plate/groove → neural folds fuse at **day 22** (starting at the hindbrain/cervical level) → **anterior neuropore closes day ~24** (lamina terminalis), **posterior neuropore day ~26** (to L1/2) → failure = **neural tube defects** (anencephaly, myelomeningocele).
**Secondary neurulation** (caudal cell mass, weeks 4–7) forms the conus/filum → tethered cord, lipomas, terminal myelocystocele.

**Premature dysjunction** (ectoderm separates too early): mesenchyme enters the neural tube → **lipomas, lipomyelomeningocele**.
**Focal failure of dysjunction:** persistent ectodermal tract → **dermal sinus tract** (± dermoid/epidermoid).

zeilen: Microcephaly, megalencephaly, vascular malformations, neurocutaneous syndromes
Lissencephaly, pachygyria, polymicrogyria, heterotopia, schizencephaly, callosal agenesis

cards.rueckseite:
Leptomeninges (pia/arachnoid), **Schwann cells**, dorsal root and cranial sensory ganglia, autonomic ganglia, **adrenal medulla**, **melanocytes**, APUD cells (→ paraganglioma, pheochromocytoma, neuroblastoma, melanoma).
Dura = mesoderm. Notochord → nucleus pulposus (and chordoma).

cards.vorderseite: Corpus callosum formation and partial agenesis
cards.rueckseite: Forms between weeks 8–17 from **front to back** (genu → body → splenium), with the **rostrum last**. Therefore partial agenesis affects the **posterior body/splenium and rostrum**, sparing the genu (exception: holoprosencephaly, where the posterior part is present).

**Posterior** and sphenoid fontanelles: 2–3 months. **Mastoid:** ~1 year. **Anterior fontanelle: ~2 (up to 2.5) years**. **Metopic suture:** first suture to close (~3–9 months; book: around the first year).

Chiari II (~100%), hydrocephalus (~80%), syringomyelia/hydromyelia (~50%), diastematomyelia (~40%), scoliosis, kyphosis, clubfoot. Risk factors: **folate deficiency, valproate, carbamazepine**, affected siblings. Elevated maternal serum **α-fetoprotein**.

**Occipital** (~80% in the West, female): associated with Chiari III, Dandy–Walker, Klippel–Feil, myelomeningocele.
**Parietal** (~10%): midline anomalies, callosal agenesis.
**Frontoethmoidal (sincipital):** Southeast Asia, not associated with neural tube defects.
**Basal (transsphenoidal, sphenoethmoidal):** occult, CSF leak, endocrine dysfunction.
**Nasal dermal sinus:** enlarged foramen cecum, bifid crista galli → dermoid.

zeilen: Monoventricle, fused thalami, no falx/interhemispheric fissure, cyclopia; trisomy 13
Partial posterior falx and fissure, partly separated thalami; hypotelorism, cleft lip
Falx and fissure present, **absent septum pellucidum**, squared frontal horns, frontal fusion
Absent septum + optic nerve hypoplasia + hypothalamic–pituitary dysfunction; often schizencephaly
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 186–187. "The face predicts the brain."

cards.rueckseite: **Dysplastic cerebellar gangliocytoma**: thickened folia with "**tiger-striped**" (striated) T2 appearance, hypertrophic granular layer; mass effect on the 4th ventricle → hydrocephalus. Associated with **Cowden syndrome (PTEN, 10q23)**: trichilemmomas, breast/thyroid/endometrial cancer, GI hamartomas.

**Hydromyelia:** dilated central canal **lined by ependyma** (Chiari II, myelomeningocele).
**Syringomyelia:** cavity separate from the central canal **lined by glia** (astrocytes).
In practice often combined: "syringohydromyelia". Syringobulbia = in the brainstem.

Both **FGFR2** mutations, autosomal dominant, multisuture (coronal) craniosynostosis, midface hypoplasia, exorbitism.
**Apert:** plus **syndactyly** of hands/feet, more severe intellectual disability.
**Crouzon:** no limb anomalies, most frequent craniofacial syndrome, hydrocephalus and Chiari I more frequent.

**Atlantoaxial instability** (transverse ligament laxity, os odontoideum) and cervical stenosis; early-onset **Alzheimer disease** (APP gene on chromosome 21); congenital heart disease (paradoxical emboli, **brain abscess**); moyamoya.

cards.vorderseite: Caput succedaneum vs. subgaleal hematoma vs. cephalohematoma
cards.rueckseite:
**Caput succedaneum:** scalp edema/hemorrhage, **crosses sutures**, resolves in ~48 h.
**Subgaleal (subaponeurotic) hemorrhage:** under the galea, crosses sutures, can cause **massive blood loss/shock** (vacuum delivery).
**Cephalohematoma:** **subperiosteal**, **limited by sutures** (usually parietal), may calcify.

zeilen: IVH with parenchymal hemorrhage (periventricular venous infarction)
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 190–191. Occurs in ~40% < 35 weeks, mostly within 72 h; germinal matrix at the caudothalamic groove involutes by ~34 weeks.

cards.rueckseite: Ischemic necrosis of the **periventricular white matter** (watershed of premature brain), esp. at the trigones and near the foramen of Monro. Risks: prematurity, hypotension, sepsis, RDS. Sequelae: **spastic diplegia** (legs > arms; corticospinal leg fibers closest to the ventricle), visual impairment; imaging: cysts, then irregular ventricles, white matter loss.

Unconjugated (unbound) bilirubin deposits in gray matter: **globus pallidus, subthalamic nucleus**, hippocampus, CN III and VIII nuclei, dentate. Sequelae: choreoathetosis, **sensorineural deafness**, upgaze palsy, dental dysplasia. Treatment: phototherapy, exchange transfusion.

zeilen: Group B streptococcus, E. coli, Listeria
N. meningitidis, S. pneumoniae (H. influenzae before vaccination)

cards.rueckseite:
- **Frontal sinus / ethmoid** → **frontal lobe**
- **Sphenoid sinus** → temporal lobe/sella
- **Otitis/mastoiditis** → **temporal lobe** or **cerebellum**
- Dental → frontal
- Hematogenous (lung, heart, cyanotic heart disease) → **multiple, gray–white junction, MCA territory**
Most common organisms: **streptococci** (S. milleri/anginosus), anaerobes; trauma/postoperative: S. aureus; neonates: Citrobacter, Proteus.

Most common cause of **sporadic** viral encephalitis (HSV-1 in adults; HSV-2 in neonates, diffuse). Spread via olfactory/trigeminal pathways → **hemorrhagic necrosis of medial temporal and orbitofrontal lobes**, often bilateral and asymmetric. CSF: lymphocytes, RBCs; **HSV PCR**; EEG: **periodic lateralized epileptiform discharges (PLEDs)**. Treat **IV acyclovir** immediately (14–21 days); untreated mortality ~70%.
cards.notiz: CNBR p. 202. Book quotes steroids + acyclovir and 50–60% mortality.

cards.rueckseite: Reactivation of **JC polyomavirus** in immunosuppressed patients (AIDS, natalizumab, rituximab, transplant). Infects **oligodendrocytes** → enlarged nuclei with ground-glass inclusions, bizarre astrocytes, demyelination. MRI: asymmetric subcortical white matter T2 lesions involving U-fibers, **no mass effect, usually no enhancement**. Treatment: restore immunity.

cards.vorderseite: Toxoplasmosis vs. CNS lymphoma in AIDS
cards.rueckseite:
**Toxoplasmosis:** most common mass lesion in AIDS; multiple **ring-enhancing** lesions in **basal ganglia** and gray–white junction ("eccentric target sign"); **thallium/PET cold**. Treat with **pyrimethamine + sulfadiazine + leucovorin**; response in 2–3 weeks.
**Primary CNS lymphoma:** often single, periventricular, crosses corpus callosum, **thallium/PET hot**, EBV in CSF. Biopsy if no response to toxo therapy.

Most common parasitic CNS infection worldwide; **Taenia solium** larvae after ingestion of **eggs** (fecal–oral; pork tapeworm itself from undercooked pork). Stages: vesicular (cyst with **scolex**, "dot in a hole") → colloidal (enhancing, edema) → granular → calcified. Presents with seizures; intraventricular cysts → hydrocephalus (endoscopic removal). Treatment: **albendazole/praziquantel + steroids**.

Most common **fungal meningitis**, from bird droppings; immunocompromised (AIDS). Diagnosis: **cryptococcal antigen** (> 90% sensitive), India ink (capsule halo), very high opening pressure (manage with serial LPs/drain). Imaging: dilated Virchow–Robin spaces, **gelatinous pseudocysts** in basal ganglia. Treatment: **amphotericin B + flucytosine**, then fluconazole.

**Aspergillus:** **septate** hyphae branching at **acute (45°) angles**; angioinvasive → hemorrhagic infarcts, abscesses; immunosuppressed; voriconazole.
**Mucor (Rhizopus):** **nonseptate** broad hyphae branching at **right angles**; **rhinocerebral** in **diabetic ketoacidosis**; invades orbit, cavernous sinus, ICA; treat with surgical debridement + **amphotericin B**.

**Basal** meningitis with thick exudate → **cranial neuropathies** (VI), **communicating hydrocephalus**, vasculitis with infarcts (basal ganglia/internal capsule). CSF: lymphocytes, **very high protein, low glucose**, low Cl⁻. Tuberculomas: ring-enhancing, "target". Treatment: multidrug (RIPE) + **dexamethasone**; shunt for hydrocephalus.

Prion disease (misfolded PrP^Sc, resistant to standard sterilization). Rapidly progressive dementia, **myoclonus**, ataxia; EEG: **periodic sharp wave complexes**; CSF **14-3-3 protein**, RT-QuIC; MRI DWI: cortical ribboning, caudate/putamen (sporadic), **pulvinar sign** (variant CJD). Pathology: **spongiform change**, neuronal loss, gliosis, no inflammation. Instruments: special decontamination (NaOH, autoclave) or disposal.
